aptitudes_semantics.absent: a work type with no board, or no observation for this model, is ABSENT from `aptitudes`, never null
aptitudes_semantics.board_coverage: boards the pinned snapshot carries, with the rows each one publishes. aptitudes_semantics.level: rank percentile inside the named board: 1 - (rank-1)/(of-1). A convenience for readers; the router orders on `score` inside one board, and a board that publishes dimensions instead of ELO has `score: null` and `method: measured-rank-only`
aptitudes_semantics.measured_disagreement: the boards disagree on the frontier: on the pinned 2026-10-07 snapshot `code` rank 1 is claude-opus-5.5-max with claude-fable-5.1-max 5th, while `agent` rank 1 is Claude Fable 5.1 (Max)

spellings: 1819 normalized names over 622 rows; 30 are claimed by more than one row, of which 10 have no exact-name owner and therefore resolve to none (deepseekaideepseekr1, deepseekaideepseekv3, deepseekflash, deepseekv4flashfree, gemini31pro, geminiprolatest, gemma4, mistralsmall, ...)

harness-declared rows: 4 models the harness exposes and models.dev publishes without a canonical id (abliteration-abliterated-model-large-v2, olafangensan-glm-4.7-flash-heretic, venice-uncensored-1-2, venice-uncensored-role-play); 2 harness ids appear in no models.dev entry at all (dolphin-mistral-24b-venice, tritech-auto) and stay outside the catalog, so the router places them by family inference. A harness id that models.dev does publish is matched through the aliases of its canonical row, which is how `<lab>/glm-5.3-flash` answers to the harness id `glm-flash-latest`

selected 360 of 626 canonical models; 475 usable (chat, priced or harness-exposed), the rest non-chat, unpriced or deprecated; harness + benchmark-covered first, then newest-per-family up to --per-family 6 within --limit 500
role: primary source of model knowledge for the routing plugin; the router intersects this catalog with what the active harness exposes, then assigns per tier

row_order.rule: tier ascending, then the declared evidence order (board priority ['code', 'text', 'vision', 'agent'], score descending inside a board, rank ascending for a rank-only board), then the model id
row_order.why: `declared_order` in the router is the row index, and `best` falls back to it when the governing board has evidence for none of the candidates. An alphabetical file made that fallback depend on the first letter of a model id

semantics.benchmark_selection: the benchmark on `tier_evidence` is chosen by board priority ['code', 'text', 'vision', 'agent'] and by score inside that board. Taking the maximum score across boards would compare separate populations.
semantics.cost_is_indicative: list prices, not what any given gateway charges. Measured divergences: Anthropic cache_write is 1.6x on the reference gateway; gemini-3.8-flash input is 0.75 there against 1.5 in models.dev and 0.825 in OpenRouter. At runtime a harness-declared value always wins.
semantics.null_policy: a missing value is null, never 0 and never a silent default
semantics.price_does_not_rank_capability: measured: gpt-6-astra-max and claude-fable-5.1-max share the price structure 10/50 and sit 43 ELO and 3 ranks apart; Spearman rho(price,score) is 0.718 within one board and -0.11 pooled.
semantics.window: input = context window in tokens, output = max completion tokens. A zero or null output limit is a marker, not a limit.

sources.licence: MIT on the mirror's files; the underlying ELO data belongs to arena.ai with no stated redistribution term, so it is used as evidence for a declared tier and not republished
sources.name: arena-ai-leaderboards (mirror of arena.ai)
supplies: aptitudes and tier evidence: rank, ELO score, 95% CI, votes, per board

tier_definition.assignment: declared by the catalog author from lab product positioning and checked against the pinned Arena board where it covers the model. Never derived from price alone, and never from a name without recorded reasoning.
tier_definition.invariance_rule: tier is a property of the model, never of the (model, effort) pair: a tier3 model stays tier3 at every thinking level
tier_definition.tier1: economy: small, cheap, high-volume, low-risk work. hop_depth 1, direct output, no invariant table.
tier_definition.tier2: workhorse: standard development and analysis work. hop_depth 1, no direct output.
tier_definition.tier3: frontier: deep work, multi-hop reasoning, adversarial review. hop_depth 2, invariant table required.
